target_task.text: Eliciting latent factual and reasoning knowledge encoded in large language models that is not faithfully reflected in their surface-level outputs.

limitation.text: Existing approaches rely on contrastive activation patterns that struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks, and mechanistic interpretability tools have primarily been used to understand model behavior rather than to extract hidden knowledge.

combination.text: By combining sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching, the framework locates knowledge-bearing representations within the large language model. It then verifies these representations using causal probing and applies representation engineering to surface the hidden knowledge without modifying model weights.

summary.text: This briefing examines an integrated method that combines sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching to elicit latent factual and reasoning knowledge from large language models. The framework locates knowledge-bearing representations, verifies them via causal probing, and surfaces hidden knowledge without modifying model weights. This approach addresses the limitation where existing contrastive methods struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks and interpretability tools are used merely to understand rather than extract hidden knowledge.

target_user.text: The target user includes AI security researchers, software engineering teams, and enterprise practitioners utilizing automated software security scanners and code fixing pipelines.

jtbd.text: When deploying large language models in complex reasoning and security tasks, developers want to reliably extract unstated or latent knowledge and verify code vulnerabilities so that they can surface hidden information without altering model weights.

value_prop.text: Unlike contrastive activation approaches that struggle with multi-step reasoning tasks, our approach uses sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching to accurately locate knowledge-bearing representations and surface hidden knowledge without modifying model weights.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption, driven by desirability (DVF axis score 2.0), is that AI practitioners and security engineers will actively demand and adopt a complex mechanistic interpretability pipeline over simpler weight-based or surface-level elicitation methods.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption on desirability, we will launch a demand landing page explaining the latent knowledge elicitation pipeline and conduct problem interviews with security engineers and AI researchers.
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: Success will be measured by a proposed threshold of 25 percent visitor conversion on the landing page and at least 15 positive problem interview sign-ups confirming a strong workflow pain point.

kill_criteria.text: The concept will be killed if fewer than a proposed threshold of 5 percent of landing page visitors express interest or if over 80 percent of interviewed engineers state they have no need to extract latent knowledge beyond standard outputs.

open_source.use: Will be used to provide automated interpretability tools that let language models know themselves through automated feature analysis.
Will be utilized for measuring internal model states and unlearning depth via activation patching.
Will be used for automated benchmarking of language model agents on software security and patching tasks.

to_build.text: A unified representation engineering module to bridge sparse autoencoder feature localization with causal probing and unweighted knowledge elicitation.
